findings.title: set_caps rewrites a surrounding-text word with DeleteSurrounding although no key was pressed (uncertain, depends on client)
findings.scenario: Surrounding-text client (no preedit) that reuses one input context for several fields (browser-style) and sends a content-type change without a prior Reset/FocusOut when focus moves to another field, e.g. a password input. The user typed `the best` (shown `the bét`) in field A, clicks into a password field B; the client sends SetContentType(password). set_caps calls ctx.flush (at_cursor=true) under the old Surrounding caps, so end_word emits DeleteSurrounding{-3,3} + Commit("best"). The cursor is now in B: 3 characters before the cursor in B are deleted and the raw keys of the previous field's word are committed into the password field. Before this change set_caps in Surrounding mode sent nothing, so the delete is new. This is the same cursor-moved hazard D13 uses to exclude reset/focus-out, but set_caps is listed among the rewriting events.
findings.evidence: ime.rs:318-328 set_caps -> ctx.flush(&mut out) -> end_word(out, true); ime.rs:183-198 Edit::Surrounding if at_cursor && finished.text != shown pushes DeleteSurrounding then Commit(finished.text). tests/word_end.rs:148-151 asserts this output for set_caps in SURROUNDING mode. decisions.md D13 lists set_caps as a rewrite event. Fix: in set_caps call ctx.flush_away (at_cursor=false), at least when the new caps are password or when the client did not send a key in between; or forget `last` and keep the shown word, as for reset.

findings.title: finish adds another unwiped heap copy of the word's letters via parse() (SEC-4 best effort)
findings.scenario: Every word end now calls parse(&self.letters, ...) once more. parse builds Vec<char> w (lib.rs:768), String cons (778) and String fin (787) from the typed letters and drops them without wiping, so each finished word leaves one more freed copy of its letters on the heap, which a later memory disclosure or core dump could expose. The pattern is the same as the per-key parse calls, so impact is small, but the new path does not meet the 'no unwiped copy' wording of SEC-4.
findings.evidence: lib.rs:363 `let Some(s) = parse(&self.letters, self.tone)` in Composer::finish; lib.rs:768 `let w: Vec<char> = letters.iter().map(|l| l.ch).collect();` with no zeroize. Fix: let parse work on a fixed-size stack array ([char; MAX] / ArrayVec) or wipe w, cons and fin before return (zeroize on Vec<char> / String).
